title: onprem/airgap: add offline bundle vendoring for RKE2 (AlmaLinux/Rocky) + rollback tooling
author: Priya Menon
release_notes:
- Adds vendored offline bundle for RKE2 targeting AlmaLinux 9 / Rocky Linux 9
- Includes improved rollback tooling for air-gapped upgrades
- Installer will now prefer vendored images when --use-vendored is enabled
description:
Motivation: Customers running the private installer in air-gapped environments have requested first-class support for vendor-supplied RKE2 bundles on AlmaLinux/Rocky variants and safer rollback semantics for failed upgrades. This PR bundles a tested set of RKE2 artifacts (rke2 binaries, images, systemd units) for AlmaLinux/Rocky, adds vendoring tooling to create repeatable offline bundles, and introduces a conservative rollback path in the installer to revert node-level changes when an upgrade fails.

Summary of changes: vendoring scripts and bundle manifests added under installer/offline-bundles/rke2/almalinux-rocky; new installer flag --use-vendored to select offline bundle at install/upgrade time; rollback helper binary redwood-rollback (lightweight, idempotent) and orchestration in the upgrade flow; Helm chart tweak to allow preloaded images to be recognized by the chart hooks.

Checklist: - [x] Vendoring scripts able to produce deterministic tarball and manifest - [x] Installer reads and validates vendored manifest signature (TUF signed snapshot) - [x] Upgrade flow integrates rollback hook and records node-level checkpoints - [x] Documentation and upgrade/rollback runbook added - [x] CI smoke tests for airgap install/upgrade on AlmaLinux and Rocky image variants

Testing: Unit + integration tests added for manifest parsing and signature validation. Manual end-to-end runs performed against AlmaLinux 9 and Rocky 9 VMs in an isolated network; initial integration run caught image path mismatch (fixed in commit 3). CI: first pipeline run failed on airgap e2e due to registry mirror timing (flake), rerun passed; full CI now green.

Backward compatibility: The default behavior is unchanged; vendored bundles are opt-in via --use-vendored. Rollback behavior is conservative and only activates during upgrade failures when --enable-rollback is specified or when running the automated upgrade command.

Related: ENG-4721 (bundle vendoring work), ENG-4789 (rollback design).

merge_commit_summary: squash: add vendored RKE2 offline bundle for AlmaLinux/Rocky, vendoring scripts, and safe rollback tooling; update docs and CI
upgrade_instructions: 1) Upload vendored tarball to the customer mirror and ensure TUF metadata is reachable by the installer.\n2) Run: ./redwood-installer --use-vendored --airgap --bundle-manifest /path/to/manifest.yaml\n3) For upgrades, run: ./redwood-installer upgrade --use-vendored --enable-rollback; if upgrade fails, run: ./redwood-rollback --bundle /path/to/backup --dry-run to preview, then without --dry-run to apply.
notes: This PR was driven by customer POC with a large financial services customer running AlmaLinux 9. The vendored bundle is intentionally conservative: we only vendor components we control and verify checksums with TUF metadata. Follow-up work: add automated pruning of obsolete bundle components (ENG-4890).
